lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: しょう、本当、よく来た、ね。
lines.en: Sho — you really did come, didn't you.
lines.style: Warm, unhurried opening. Low, steady voice with country-road ease. Genuine pleasure threaded underneath — not performative. A gentle settling-in, the kind of welcome that makes someone feel they belong.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: うん、本当、嬉しい、本当に。
lines.en: Yeah — I'm really happy to be here.
lines.style: Small, genuine voice. Soft and sincere without straining. A six-year-old's natural warmth — not trying to sound grown-up. Quiet appreciation that feels entirely true.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.jp: 優しい、お客さん、本当に。
lines.style: Observational, almost to himself. Warm country cadence. A quiet compliment that lands because it's not forced — the kind of thing an older person says when they've noticed something real about someone.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Being together like this — it's really fun.
lines.style: Small voice, bright beneath the gentleness. Direct and uncomplicated. A six-year-old speaking a simple truth with the whole of his small heart — no embellishment needed.

lines.speaker: tatsuya_country
lines.style: Closing warmth, almost a soft promise. Low and steady. Not a command but a genuine invitation — the kind of thing someone says when they mean it and will remember you came.
